Network and VPC peering / private deployments

transcript:
[00:00:00] Jamie Ortiz: Okay good morning everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the marketplace integration and the reference arch for the joint solution. uh feel free to interrupt, lots to cover.
[00:00:18] Liam Chen: Yep thanks Jamie, from AuroraCloud side we've got Sofia and Ethan here. we're mainly looking to understand how Redwood wants the listing laid out and what integration points we need for single-sign on and billing.
[00:00:30] Priya Mehta: Hi all, Priya from Redwood infra. quick agenda: marketplace checklist, RA layers, network options (hosted/dedicated/private), security, and handoffs.
[00:00:45] Sofia Garcia: Quick note, we have marketplace timelines - product marketing wants a listing by mid-June so need to lock the RA and copy by early May.
[00:00:55] Jamie Ortiz: OK that timeline makes sense. Priya, can you start on the checklist please? what do partners typically need to provide?
[00:01:06] Priya Mehta: sure, so typical requirements: manifest (name, description, screenshots), onboarding flow notes, test accounts, IAM/roles for provisioning, billing SKU mapping, and security docs (SOC 2 summary, SSO metadata). also we have a short RA template that shows deployment variants. i'll share the checklist link in follow-up - it's on our partner portal, eg https://redwood.example.com/marketplace-checklist
[00:01:30] Ethan Brooks: when you say IAM, do you need full service account keys or can we do scoped roles and short-lived tokens? we prefer not to hand over long-lived keys.
[00:01:40] Priya Mehta: absolutely scoped roles and OIDC flow preferred. for hosted integration we typically do a service account with limited permissions or an OAuth/OIDC service connection; for private deployments we do peering and customer managed KMS.
[00:01:55] Liam Chen: and networking - what's the recommended approach for AuroraCloud? we have customers that want VPC peering and some that are ok with hosted options.
[00:02:06] Priya Mehta: right, we support three patterns: (1) Redwood Hosted API - easiest, no peering, uses standard API keys and RBAC; (2) Dedicated - reserved capacity in a shared VPC with firewall rules; (3) Private (VPC/on-prem) - customer-managed network, peering, or private link. for marketplace listing we want you to document which modes you support and any restrictions.
[00:02:30] Sofia Garcia: ok good. can the RA include an example terraform snippet for peering and IAM? that helps our platform docs.
[00:02:38] Priya Mehta: yes will include snippet. note — sometimes terraform module names get mis-typed in our docs, sorry, i mean we'll include a cleaned up example.
[00:02:48] Jamie Ortiz: let's talk about SSO - AuroraCloud customers expect SAML, OIDC, SCIM provisioning. what's Redwood's stance?
[00:02:56] Priya Mehta: we support SAML and OIDC for SSO, and SCIM for user provisioning in Console (for RBAC). for marketplace launches we ask partners to provide SSO metadata and a test tenant.
[00:03:10] Ethan Brooks: SOC 2 is a hard requirement for some of our enterprise customers. is Redwood SOC 2 compliant? and what logs do you expose?
[00:03:18] Jamie Ortiz: yes Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; we'll share the attestation as part of the security pack. we also provide audit logs, per-route traces, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[00:03:30] Priya Mehta: small note, audit logs retention defaults to 90 days for the console; extended retention is an add-on. also you can enable HSM/KMS integrations in private deployments.
[00:03:40] Liam Chen: perfect. on billing - we need to map SKUs to marketplace product IDs and ensure metering. how does Redwood expose usage/metrics?
[00:03:50] Priya Mehta: we expose token-level usage and per-route metrics via our billing API. for marketplace we can provide a CSV mapping example and a webhook for usage exports. we'll need your SKU list so we can align IDs.
[00:04:05] Sofia Garcia: i'll pull the SKU/pricing spreadsheet and share after the call.
[00:04:09] Jamie Ortiz: great. Priya, can you run through the RA high level?
[00:04:13] Priya Mehta: sure, RA has three layers: frontend onboarding and provisioning, control plane for routing and model selection, and the runtime layer (serving GPU pools). for joint solutions we typically show two deployment options: integrated hosted flow where Aurora uses Redwood-hosted endpoints, and private flow where Aurora customers get a VPC connector and reserved capacity. i'll sketch both, include network diagrams and security callouts.
[00:04:40] Liam Chen: any performance notes? we have customers worried about latency when going through a marketplace integration.
[00:04:46] Priya Mehta: yes we should call out latency SLAs and optional dedicated capacity. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quantization profiles per customer workload; we can include a recommended profile for low-latency agents vs bulk batch jobs. small caveat: quantization may affect quality so we include eval guidance.
[00:05:05] Ethan Brooks: on data residency and logs, customers often need everything to remain in their region. do you support region pinning?
[00:05:12] Priya Mehta: yes region pinning for hosted routes, and private deployments let you run in-region. mention in the listing which regions are supported.
[00:05:21] Jamie Ortiz: there was a question earlier about artifacts - i'll share the checklist and a sample RA doc after the call; link will go to the drive folder (drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123) and to the partner portal.
[00:05:36] Sofia Garcia: perfect. one operational question: what is the expected onboarding timeline for a partner? from signed agreement to listing?
[00:05:44] Jamie Ortiz: typically 4-8 weeks depending on integration depth: 2-3 weeks for listing copy + assets + security review if using hosted; 4-8 weeks if private deployment and certs/peering are required.
[00:05:58] Priya Mehta: and security questionnaires can add time; Ethan, if you share your questionnaire we can do a preliminary pass and point to our SOC2 and encryption docs.
[00:06:08] Ethan Brooks: will do, i'll also include our cloud architecture notes so you can align the RA.
[00:06:12] Liam Chen: any blockers from Redwood side?
[00:06:15] Priya Mehta: no blockers, just dependencies: SKU/pricing CSV, test accounts for SSO, and security questionnaire. once we have those we can produce the RA draft and a terraform snippet.
[00:06:26] Jamie Ortiz: ok let's recap next steps — i'll send checklist now, Priya will draft RA and terraform snippet, Liam will send SKU and security doc, Ethan will send questionnaire. we'll schedule a RA review for the week of May 2nd.
[00:06:40] Sofia Garcia: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[00:06:43] Jamie Ortiz: thanks all, talk soon.
